chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Jazz becoming white in schools; the danger of exclusiveness
summary: Johnston worries young people learn jazz through white examples. Gil points to Black professors and warns against exclusiveness.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Yes. (LAUGHTER). That's a good pun. (LAUGHTER). But I think there is something else involved and that is respectability. Because as I see it, jazz is getting more and more white. And

one of the things that bothered me so when I, while I spent the time in Washington reviewing proposals, was that the white schools are bringing in bands such as Stan Kanton's and he seems to be the most in demand for jazz workshops as such. And the point is to teach young people, this is what the proposals say, to teach young people about jazz. And yet there is no historical perspective included in these proposals.
So that young people who are now just learning about jazz, it seems to me, are learning it almost in white terms only. And this does bother me. Because I think.....
By terms, you mean by example....
By example, and they don't know the derivation of it. And.....

There always has been, there is and there always will be people who are looking for the great white hope. There is always that kind of group. It's so silly that, you know, all of a sudden it's there and you say what? Anyway, that's being counter-acted also because for example, Dizzy is going to be Professor of Music at Yale, right? and Archie and what do you call him, Max Roach went to the University of Massachusetts? Right?
And Dave Baker is out at (Indiana?)
That's right, so it's all going to be counter-acted. by authentic... Not that a lot of white people are not good or genuine about it.

They have genuine taste. Because I'm one. I have genuine taste. I say they all the time because I don't feel black or white. I don't feel like, I tried, I haven't tried, I just like skirted around that one. Because if I didn't skirt around it, I'd be missing out on things in life.

That's right. That's my thing. That's what I can't stand about exclusiveness. I think that is the road to oblivion. Totally, all exclusiveness, they get carried chronically and end up in oblivion......(VOICE FADES OUT).
